cards.explanation: The answer is the LORD's command. The verse says Joshua gave Caleb his portion "According to the LORD’s command to him…" So Joshua isn't making this up as he goes. He's handing out the land the way he was told, kind of like me following a recipe card instead of guessing at the flour (Joshua 15:13).

The answer is that he drives them out. The verse says Caleb "…drove out from there the three sons of Anak…" the descendants of Sheshai, Ahiman, and Talmai. Three of them, and Caleb drove them out. I can't even drive the crumbs off my counter, and they're not even big (Joshua 15:14).

The word is daughter. Caleb says, "To the man who strikes down Kiriath-sepher and captures it, I will give my daughter Acsah in marriage." That's a big promise to put on the table, friends. I think a man who says that out loud means to keep it (Joshua 15:16).

The answer is False. The text says Othniel captured the city, and then "…Caleb gave his daughter Acsah to him in marriage." No backing out, no excuses, no "let me think about it." Caleb did just what he said he would (Joshua 15:17).

The answer is that Caleb asks what she desires. When Acsah gets off her donkey, Caleb asks her, "What do you desire?" Short and kind, and it opens the door for her to ask, friends. I'd say that's a dad who wants to hear her out (Joshua 15:18).

The answer is True! Acsah asks for springs of water, and Caleb doesn't hold back. The verse says "So Caleb gave her both the upper and lower springs." She asked, and she got the upper and the lower. I think that's a dad who loves saying yes (Joshua 15:19).

The answer is that Judah can't drive them out. The text says "…the descendants of Judah could not drive out the Jebusites living in Jerusalem." It's a little hard to read after all those cities, friends, but it's honest. The verse says that to this day the Jebusites live there among the descendants of Judah (Joshua 15:63).

The answer is True. The verse says, "…to this day the Jebusites live there among the descendants of Judah." So at the time of writing, they were still in Jerusalem. The list ends on that note, plain and honest, friends (Joshua 15:63).
